question: A sum of ₹2,500 becomes ₹3,000 in 4 years at simple interest. What is the rate of interest?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interest = 3000 − 2500 = 500

⇒ 4 years interest = 500

⇒ 1 year interest = 500 ÷ 4 = 125

⇒ Rate = (125 ÷ 2500) × 100 = 5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = 2500

Amount (A) = 3000

Time (T) = 4 years

**Formula:**

Simple Interest (SI) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Calculations:**

⇒ SI = A − P = 3000 − 2500 = 500

⇒ 500 = (2500 × R × 4) ÷ 100

⇒ 500 = 100R

⇒ R = 5%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

**SI Formula:** SI = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

**Amount Relation:** A = P + SI

**Unitary Method:** Find 1 year interest, then compute rate

**Shortcut Tip:** Rate = (SI × 100) ÷ (P × T)
